samf-senior-1997-r2-01.title: Work backwards
samf-senior-1997-r2-01.body:
Half the number is $25+8=33$, so the number is $66$.

**Answer: (E) 66**

samf-senior-1997-r2-02.title: Pigeonhole principle
samf-senior-1997-r2-02.body:
There are only 3 colours, so 3 socks could all be different. A fourth sock must repeat a colour, so 4 socks guarantee a matching pair.

**Answer: (C) 4**

samf-senior-1997-r2-03.title: Subtract the white triangle
samf-senior-1997-r2-03.body:
The rectangle has area $12\times7=84$. The white triangle has base 12 and height 7, so its area is $\frac12\cdot12\cdot7=42$. The shaded area is $84-42=42$.

**Answer: (B) 42**

samf-senior-1997-r2-04.title: One of each kind
samf-senior-1997-r2-04.body:
One coin of each kind is worth $2+5+10+50+100=167$ cents $=$ R1.67. The total is R10.02 $=1002$ cents, and $1002\div167=6$. So she has 6 coins of each kind, i.e. $6\times5=30$ coins.

**Answer: (E) 30**

samf-senior-1997-r2-05.title: Pythagoras twice
samf-senior-1997-r2-05.body:
In right triangle $ABC$: $AC^2=10^2-6^2=64$, so $AC=8$. In right triangle $ACD$: $AD^2=8^2+15^2=64+225=289$, so $AD=17$.

**Answer: (A) 17**

samf-senior-1997-r2-06.title: Bound the volume
samf-senior-1997-r2-06.body:
The third side lies between 50 cm and 90 cm. So the volume lies between $50\times50\times90=225\,000$ and $50\times90\times90=405\,000$ cm$^3$. Only $360\,000$ is in this range.

**Answer: (D) 360 000**

samf-senior-1997-r2-07.title: Equilateral triangles
samf-senior-1997-r2-07.body:
Joining the centre to the vertices splits the hexagon into 6 equilateral triangles whose sides equal the radius $r$. The hexagon's perimeter is $6r$ and the circle's circumference is $2\pi r$. The ratio is $2\pi r:6r=\pi:3$.

**Answer: (D) $\pi:3$**

samf-senior-1997-r2-08.title: Write the number as $10m+n$
samf-senior-1997-r2-08.body:
$(10m+n)-(m+n)=9m=45$, so $m=5$ and $n$ can be any digit $0,\dots,9$. The numbers are $50,51,\dots,59$: ten numbers.

**Answer: (E) 10**

samf-senior-1997-r2-10.title: Divisors of 1956
samf-senior-1997-r2-10.body:
A number $d$ leaves remainder 41 on dividing 1997 exactly when $d>41$ and $d\mid1997-41=1956$. Now $1956=2^2\cdot3\cdot163$, whose divisors are $1,2,3,4,6,12,163,326,489,652,978,1956$. Those greater than 41 are $163,326,489,652,978,1956$: six numbers.

**Answer: (A) 6**

samf-senior-1997-r2-11.title: Pythagoras with the centres
samf-senior-1997-r2-11.body:
Let $R$ be the radius. In the figure the centre $C$ of the upper semicircle is on the top edge and the centre $O$ of the lower one is on the bottom edge, with $OC=2R$ (the semicircles touch). Horizontally the centres are $160-2R$ apart and vertically $80$ apart, so $(2R)^2=80^2+(160-2R)^2$. Expanding, $4R^2=6400+25600-640R+4R^2$, so $640R=32000$ and $R=50$. The diameter is $100$ cm.

**Answer: (D) 100**

samf-senior-1997-r2-12.title: Compare the two sides
samf-senior-1997-r2-12.body:
For every real $x$, $\sqrt{x^4+16}>\sqrt{x^4}=x^2>x^2-4$, so the two sides are never equal. There are no solutions. (Squaring would give $x^4+16=x^4-8x^2+16$, i.e. $x=0$, but $x=0$ fails: $\sqrt{16}=4\neq-4$.)

**Answer: (A) 0**

samf-senior-1997-r2-13.title: Similar triangles
samf-senior-1997-r2-13.body:
Tangents are perpendicular to radii, so the angles at $T$ and $D$ are right angles. $AB=3+2=5$ and $AD=3$ (it is a radius, and $AD\perp BD$), so $BD=\sqrt{25-9}=4$. Triangles $BTC$ and $BDA$ are similar (common angle at $B$, right angles at $T$ and $D$), so $\dfrac{TC}{DA}=\dfrac{BT}{BD}=\dfrac24$, giving $TC=\frac32$. Tangent lengths from $C$ to the circle with centre $A$ are equal: $CD=CT=\frac32$.

**Answer: (B) $\frac32$**

samf-senior-1997-r2-14.title: Coordinates
samf-senior-1997-r2-14.body:
Put $C=(0,0)$, $A=(0,4)$, $B=(b,0)$. Then $D=(\frac b2,0)$ and $E=(\frac b2,2)$. $AD\perp CE$: $\overrightarrow{AD}=(\frac b2,-4)$ and $\overrightarrow{CE}=(\frac b2,2)$ have dot product $\frac{b^2}4-8=0$, so $b^2=32$. Then $AB^2=b^2+16=48$ and $AB=4\sqrt3$.

**Answer: (E) $4\sqrt3$**

samf-senior-1997-r2-14.title: Similar triangles
samf-senior-1997-r2-14.body:
$E$ is the circumcentre of the right triangle, so $EC=EA=EB$. Let $\angle DAC=\alpha$; then $\angle DCE=\alpha$ (as $AD\perp CE$) and $\angle ABC=\angle ECB=\alpha$. Triangles $ACD$ and $BCA$ are similar, so $\frac{AC}{BC}=\frac{CD}{AC}$, with $CD=\frac12BC$: $BC^2=2AC^2=32$. Then $AB^2=32+16=48$.

**Answer: (E) $4\sqrt3$**

samf-senior-1997-r2-15.title: Three terms work, two do not
samf-senior-1997-r2-15.body:
Three terms suffice: $\frac12+\frac14+\frac1{60}=\frac{30+15+1}{60}=\frac{46}{60}=\frac{23}{30}$. Suppose two terms worked: $\frac1p+\frac1q=\frac{23}{30}$ with $p\ge q$. Then $\frac2q\ge\frac{23}{30}$, so $q\le\frac{60}{23}<3$, so $q=2$ (since $q=1$ gives $1>\frac{23}{30}$). But then $\frac1p=\frac{23}{30}-\frac12=\frac4{15}$ and $p=\frac{15}4$, not an integer. One term is impossible because $\frac{23}{30}$ is not a unit fraction. So the minimum is $n=3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

samf-senior-1997-r2-17.title: Allowed cut positions
samf-senior-1997-r2-17.body:
Let the string have length 1. The longer piece is at least 3 times the shorter exactly when the shorter piece is at most $\frac14$, i.e. the cut is within $\frac14$ of one of the two ends. That is $\frac14+\frac14=\frac12$ of the string.

**Answer: (D) $\frac12$**

samf-senior-1997-r2-20.title: Find the radius
samf-senior-1997-r2-20.body: The chord $XY=3$ subtends $120^\circ$ at the point $P$ of the other circle's arc, so it subtends $360^\circ-2\cdot120^\circ=120^\circ$ at the centre $C$ of the circle containing the arc (the reflex angle at the centre is $240^\circ$). Thus triangle $CXY$ has apex angle $120^\circ$ and base 3: $R=\dfrac{3/2}{\sin60^\circ}=\sqrt3$.

samf-senior-1997-r2-20.title: Lens area
samf-senior-1997-r2-20.body:
The shaded lens consists of two equal circular segments, each cut off by chord $XY$ with central angle $120^\circ$. One segment = sector $-$ triangle $=\frac13\pi R^2-\frac12R^2\sin120^\circ=\pi-\frac12\cdot3\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}2=\pi-\frac{3\sqrt3}4$. The lens is twice this: $2\left(\pi-\frac34\sqrt3\right)$.

**Answer: (E) $2\left(\pi-\frac34\sqrt3\right)$**
